description.narrative: Denna insats genom Världsbankens TF syftar till att bidra till att bygga och stärka socialt skydd och arbetsmarknadssystem i utvecklingsländerna, nämligen i Afrika. Insatsen avser system för social trygghet, socialförsäkring och arbetsmarknadsprogram. Det övergripande målet är att förbättra de fattigas motståndskraft mot oväntade katastrofer och kriser.

The proposed intervention is relevant to the broader objective of fighting poverty and strengthening of institutions in order to ensure a better and rapid response to crisis and emergencies. The programme will also assist in building up efficient social protection and labor systems to help the poor and vulnerable and to mitigate the harmful effects of crises in a coherent manner.

title.narrative: Amendment of agreement between Sida and World Bank Rapid Social Response 2020
Beslut om ändring av avtal mellan Sida och World Bank Rapid Social Response 2020

description.narrative:
The Rapid Social Response Multi-donor Trust Fund (RSR-MDTF) was designed as a response to meet the effects of the financial crises in 2008-2009 and a tool to further enhance the implementation of the Social Protection and Jobs sector strategy also known as the SPJ Compass 2012-2022. It had renewed interest in 2019-2020 and a parallel Trust Fund was established under an RSR Adaptive Umbrella Trust Fund (RSR-ADSP) as a response to the COVID-19 crisis. The RSR-MDTF/RSR-ADSP (RSR) have thematic windows for example a classical window and thematic windows for gender, youth and food security.
According to the World Bank(WB) the RSR-MDTF/RSR-ADSP has since 2009 channeled grants for 384 activities in 100 countries. These grant activities, funded through 21 rounds of calls for proposals, have been catalytic, supporting roughly $17 billion in World Bank operational financing around the globe. The systems reviews, studies and development of capacity and technical know-how has formed the basis for designing and implementing large-scale social protection programmes that has reached an estimated 176 million people.The latest call for proposals (round 21) was undertaken in 2023.
A few highlights from the narrative report are mentioned below providing examples of results achieved:
More than $16 million has been awarded in 64 grants to tackle gender-specific sources of vulnerability and expand women's and girls opportunities in more than 40 countries. A majority of the RSR gender support is implemented in Africa (35 activities, or 47 percent), while maintaining a worldwide presence.
Key themes among the RSR gender grants include interventions to boost female labor force participation and women's economic inclusion, investments toward more sex-disagregated social protection data, work to prevent GBV and link social protection beneficiaries to survivor services, and approaches to tackle women's care burdens including child and elder care. Also, the RSR- gender window has supported 26 activities designed to enhance women's economic empowerment.
-In the Democratic Republic of Congo the grant supported the Government in ensuring an efficient and gender-sensitive social response to the Ebola crisis. The grant helped produce an impact evaluation through a gender lens, and facilitated knowledge generation and dissemination on social protection in contexts of fragility and conflict.
-In Gambia, Ghana. Nigeria and Zambia RSR supported the operationalisation of the Women's Empowerment Agenda. The results can be found in a dashboard of Women and Girls Empowerment (WGE) Interventions in a user friendly repository of five WGE interventions in Africa, including information on operational details, impact evaluation and results.
- and in Zambia the grant facilitated gender-responsive design improvements in the Girls Education and Women's Empowerment and Livelihood Project (GEWEL), which Sida is co-financing bilaterally.
The RSR gender window has also provided essential funding for the creation and utilization of global knowledge products, supported the creation of the first internal platform within the World Bank, and developed a Gender Data Portal, with the support of the RSR, which makes the latest gender statistics accessible through narratives and data visualizations.
The RSR also supports policy development, for example in 2021 publishing the book "Safety first - how to leverage social safety nets to prevent gender based violence". The book has supported learning and discussion on key issues on social protection and GBV.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
